summary: A static field is shared by the whole class, and a static method is called on the class itself. Fields set on this belong to one object.
notes: static count = 0; exists once on Student, no matter how many objects you make.
maya.school is undefined. Static fields live on the class, not on its objects, so always write Student.school.
leo.school = ... adds a regular field to leo only. Student.school stays the same.
pitfall: Writing this.count++ in the constructor leaves Student.count at 0. this.count starts as undefined, so this.count++ gives NaN on that one object.
contrast: JavaScript marks shared members static like Java, but an object cannot read them: maya.school is undefined, while Python and Java both let you read the shared value through an object.
